summary: 197370948e makes all four floatx80_to_int{32,64}[_rtz]_nds helpers saturate: the out-of-range branch now returns `r < 0 ? INT32_MIN : INT32_MAX` (resp. INT64). The code delta is exactly four lines, one per helper, and nothing else. NaN takes the MAX arm because `r < 0` is false for NaN, matching softfloat. helper_fscale still reads the value UNGUARDED at :3188, which is correct rather than a gap: pass 1 offered clamping at the consumer as the alternative and warned it would leave the hard/soft divergence in place for any future caller. The lane fixed the conversion instead.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario -- a guest FSCALE with finite |ST1| >= 2^31 getting scalbn(ST0, INT32_MIN) -> +/-0 where x87 requires +/-inf, and the answer differing between the Android 'Native Floats (JIT)' setting on and off -- can no longer occur. floatx80_to_int32_round_to_zero(ST1) now returns INT32_MAX for the positive case, so floatx80_scalbn(ST0, INT32_MAX) gives +/-inf, which is both the x87-correct masked-overflow result and what the soft path gives. The hard-vs-soft divergence is gone rather than hidden.
evidence: FIVE independent legs. (1) Softfloat parity read at source, not taken from pass 1: fpu/softfloat-parts.c.inc partsN(float_to_sint) returns r=max for qNaN and sNaN (:1233-1239), r = p->sign ? min : max for infinity (:1241-1244), and min/max for negative/positive normal overflow (:1263-1271). The hard path now matches on every case. (2) EXECUTED docs/testing/x87_conv_check.py at BOTH refs: 35 assertions 0 failed at the lane head with the aarch64 cross-compile clean, and 35 assertions 13 FAILED at 622183271b, the commit that introduced the defect. The 13 are exactly positive overflow x5, NaN x4, +2^70 and rtz +2^70, and the two FSCALE +2^40 rows. ALL ELEVEN ROUNDING-MODE ROWS PASS ON BOTH SIDES, EVERY NEGATIVE-OVERFLOW ROW PASSES ON BOTH SIDES, and both exactness rows pass on both sides -- so the failures isolate the defective half and nothing else. I derived the expected count of 13 from the defect before running and it matched. (3) The carve is the shipped text and cannot diverge by a conditional: it is `git show <ref>:target/i386/tcg/fpu_helper.c` sliced by line-start markers, byte-identical from the fix to head (sha256 70eab9681e898307b9b5, 123 lines at both 197370948e and 6efac9c808), contains all four helper bodies, and contains NO PREPROCESSOR CONDITIONALS AT ALL. (4) The stub is faithful where fidelity is load-bearing: the inv= half of every assertion depends on float_raise, and the stub's definition is include/fpu/softfloat.h:104-107 verbatim; its float_round_nearest_even/down/up/to_zero = 0/1/2/3 and float_flag_invalid = 0x0001 match include/fpu/softfloat-types.h:147-165. (5) The remediation cannot leak saturation to a guest store, which would have been a NEW defect since saturation is not the x87-architectural FIST result: helper_fistl_ST0 (:1073), helper_fistll_ST0 (:1086), helper_fisttl_ST0 (:1113) and helper_fisttll_ST0 (:1126) all overwrite on float_flag_invalid; helper_fist_ST0 (:1058) and helper_fistt_ST0 (:1099) overwrite on `val != (int16_t)val`, which both saturated values trip since (int16_t)INT32_MAX == -1 and (int16_t)INT32_MIN == 0; and helper_fbst_ST0 (:1631) trips its +/-1e18 test on INT64_MAX and INT64_MIN alike.
remediation: None required.
note: Residual divergences, checked and unobservable or already dispositioned. softfloat also sets float_flag_invalid_cvti and float_flag_invalid_snan; grep finds ZERO readers of either anywhere in target/i386/, so there is nothing to diverge. The missing float_flag_inexact does have a reader (fpu_helper.c:900, mapping to FPUS_PE) but that is the documented KNOWN INCOMPLETE the other chain's P2 closed as documented-not-fixed, and 197370948e does not change it.

summary: NO REMEDIATION COMMIT EXISTS. `git diff --numstat 082878a1ca7..6efac9c808` does not list hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/psh.c at all -- the file has not been touched since pass 1's head. apply_border_adjustment(ps, vars, i, "dotSTR%d") is still at psh.c:2356 and the sign reads `dotSTR%d.x >= 0.0` and `.y >= 0.0` are still at :2377-2378, twenty lines later.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario survives verbatim. remapBorderCube (psh.c:1673) still does not scale in place: it projects to the dominant face, remaps (s,t), and reconstructs a direction with the major axis forced to +/-1.0. So with a border enabled, `.x` is the sign of the major axis rather than of dot_{i-2}, and the measured rule -- stated in terms of the raw dot signs -- is not the rule the shader evaluates. The secondary half also survives: with a border the outermost texel IS the border ring, so K = 1 - 1/8192 lands there rather than on the logical corner even when the signs are right.
evidence: Absence established two ways rather than by reading alone: psh.c is absent from the numstat of 082878a1ca7..6efac9c808, and `grep -n textureLod hw/xbox/nv2a/pgraph/glsl/psh.c` returns nothing on either branch. No decision is logged anywhere either: the lane branch carries no docs/audits/ directory, and no file on it mentions M1, M2 or this audit. The brief asked whether the fix merely moved the read -- there is no fix to ask that of. One fact pass 1 could not have: the campaign branch does not carry 4a08abef66 at all (psh.c:3120-3141 at 6817aea04e still passes the whole direction in, with neither the sign step nor DOT_STR_3D_K), so M1 is entirely confined to the unfolded work and nothing in the campaign branch is exposed today. The fold is the moment it becomes live.
remediation: Still pass 1's: read the signs BEFORE apply_border_adjustment, or capture them into locals ahead of the call. Needs dispatching to whoever holds glsl/psh.c; not mine to patch. AGENTS.md:145 -- every HIGH and MEDIUM is remediated before the code folds in.

summary: NO REMEDIATION COMMIT EXISTS, same absence as M1. psh.c:2380 is still `vec4 t%d = texture(texSamp%d, dotSTR%dDir);` -- an implicit-LOD fetch. There is no textureLod anywhere in the file on either branch.
scenario: Pass 1's scenario survives verbatim. The coordinate dotSTR%dDir still takes exactly four values, so the screen-space derivative the sampler derives its mip level from is identically zero inside a sign region and ~2K across a boundary. On a mipmapped cube that pins LOD 0 everywhere inside a region regardless of minification, and selects the coarsest level (1x1 on a full chain) on the single quad that straddles a sign change. Both behaviours are new relative to the old smoothly-varying coordinate.
evidence: Same evidence as M1: psh.c absent from the post-pass-1 numstat; no textureLod in the file; no logged decision on the lane branch. Confined to the unfolded work -- the campaign branch's DOT_STR_3D case at psh.c:3120-3141 has no step function and therefore no LOD problem.
remediation: Still pass 1's one-call fix, textureLod(..., 0.0), available on all three targets pgraph_glsl_append_version emits. NOTE THE HONEST WEAKNESS, unchanged since pass 1: whether silicon's DOT_STR_3D cube fetch uses LOD 0 or a computed level is not established anywhere in the record, so this picks the level that matches the derivation rather than one that was measured. That is not an argument for leaving M2 open -- the current code takes a level nobody chose at all -- but whoever implements it should say which level silicon fetches, or say that it is unmeasured.

summary: REFUTED by lane.skew44 from data already on disk. Not re-audited, per the brief; disposition confirmed on [issue.44].
scenario: Does not arise. The instrument pass 1 believed unavailable was already running: the FIFO_SKEW_SCAN_MAX_WORDS bail counter rides the fifoskew line as `big=` and fifo_skew_report.py already parses it, so 'the scan kept giving up' was directly measurable and is measured.
decision: Quoted from [issue.44]: "REFUTED BY THE SAME LANE AND THE REFUTATION IS BETTER THAN THE FINDING: the SCAN_MAX_WORDS bail counter already rides the fifoskew line as big= and fifo_skew_report.py already parses it. Measured on every mode-2 run on disk, big/scan_n is 0.0044% on Galleon, 0.0077% on Crimson, 0.0134% on the Texture border disc -- three orders of magnitude from a scan that bails, so 'the scan kept giving up' is not what produced the cost. Mode 2 also never reads held/kicks = 1.0000 on any workload (0.9481 / 0.7026 / 0.0370); only mode 1 does. AND THE PRIOR IN M4 IS THE DISC'S, NOT THE WORKLOAD'S: 148,704 submissions for 180 draws is the test disc, where 96.3% of segments are skipped; Galleon skips 5.2% and runs 94.2%/93.2% draw-carrying. A mode-2 cost near mode 1's on a title is therefore EXPECTED and is a property of the workload rather than of the instrument."
remediation: None. The refutation is the stronger document and pass 1's counter-example turns out to be a disc ratio read as a workload ratio.

summary: `inv_beta_mult = max_beta_mult - beta_mult` is an unsigned subtraction whose non-underflow depends entirely on `beta->beta = parameter & 0x7f800000` at pgraph/pgraph.c:1951, in another translation unit. There is no assert. This is the GL counterpart of the blit audit's M1, but WEAKER, and the difference is worth stating precisely.
scenario: If the pgraph.c mask were ever widened -- and pgraph.c's own comment signposts that world, "only 8 fractional bits are actually implemented in hardware" -- then beta_mult > 0x7f80 wraps inv_beta_mult to a huge uint32 and `b = d[x*4+ch] * inv_beta_mult` overflows silently. Not currently reachable by any guest, since no guest can defeat the mask; not guarded, so it fails silently rather than loudly.
evidence: Verified that the exactness half of Vulkan M1 has NO GL analogue. Vulkan approximates /255 as (W * 0x8081) >> 23, exact only for W < 2^16, largest reachable 65,152 against first failure 66,299 -- 1.76% headroom. GL uses a genuine uint32_t division by max_beta_mult, so there is no exactness cliff at all; its only bound is uint32 overflow of `a + b + 16320`, whose largest reachable value I measured exhaustively at 8,339,520 -- 0.19% of 2^32, about 515x headroom. GL also has NO NEON path in blit.c, so Vulkan M1's 'the two paths would be wrong differently' hazard has no GL analogue. AND the cross-module dependency IS now named: blit.c:107 says 'beta is masked with 0x7f800000 in pgraph.c', which is exactly the cheaper remediation Vulkan M1 offered as an alternative to the assert.
remediation: `assert(beta_mult <= max_beta_mult);` at the top of the BLEND_AND branch. Not implied by the condition it would sit under -- beta_mult is a dereference of state written in another translation unit and nothing in perform_blit()'s control flow constrains it -- and not a guest-input assert turned into a DoS, since the mask means no guest can reach it. Defensibly declinable: the comment already gives a mask change a thread to pull, which is why this is LOW and not a repeat of M1.

summary: The #84 refusal warns through a function-local `static bool warned`, so it fires once per process for the FIRST offending bytes_per_pixel and never again, and the message names only that value.
scenario: A title issues a Y8 BLEND_AND (warned, message says '1 bytes/pixel') and later an R5G6B5 one. The second blend is silently skipped with no output, and anyone reading the log concludes only the Y8 path was reached. The blend being skipped is the intended, documented behaviour; the invisibility of the second format is the defect. Also a plain non-atomic `static bool` on a path reachable from the vcpu thread, though a duplicated warning line is the worst that costs.
evidence: blit.c:66-76. The pattern is copied from pgraph_vk_solid_line(), which the blit pass-1 audit cited as the precedent to follow, so this is inherited rather than invented -- and the precedent has the same property.
remediation: A three-bit bitmap of warned widths, or include the format name and accept one line per format. Defensibly declinable as consistency with the existing solid_line precedent; if declined, log that.

summary: The M3 fix is SILENT when `ninja -C build -t deps` yields nothing. `.deps` ends up empty (the redirect creates it, and awk exits 0 on empty input so the `|| :` fallback never fires), the per-header `while read obj` loop gets no input, `hit` stays 0, and NO HEADER ENTERS THE INTERSECTION -- with nothing printed to say so.
scenario: A gate run whose build directory has no dependency log -- a freshly configured build/, or one after `ninja -t clean` wiped .ninja_deps -- silently returns to exactly M3's behaviour, headers dropped from the delta with every line of output looking normal. LOW because it is not reachable in a real gate run: gate.sh invokes `ninja -C build qemu-system-i386` itself at :92, so ninja and build/ necessarily exist and the build populates the deps log before the delta block runs. The severity is in the failure MODE, not the reachability.
evidence: Read at gate.sh:178-181. The contrast is internal to the same commit: the L7 fix two hunks earlier DOES print '(denominator unavailable)' when ninja cannot answer (:146-148), so the pattern was available and was not applied here. Established on this host, where ninja is absent and build/ does not exist, that the empty-.deps state is what you get.
remediation: `[ -s "$OUT/.deps" ] || echo 'NOTE: no ninja dependency data; header warnings are NOT in this delta' | tee -a "$LOG"`. One line, and it makes the one silence M3 was about impossible to repeat.

summary: objs() greps only 'Compiling C object', never 'Compiling C++ object', so a C++ object never enters .objs_prev/.objs_this -- while COMPILES (:99) and the new OBJS denominator (:142) both count C and C++.
scenario: A header included only by C++ translation units can never satisfy the new 'any object depending on it was compiled in both runs' test, so its warnings stay out of the delta. A narrow residual of M3 rather than a reopening: the tree's warning-carrying headers are overwhelmingly C, and the fix demonstrably works for those.
evidence: gate.sh:159 against :99 and :142. 4020fa286f's own L7 rationale states the asymmetry explicitly -- 'COMPILES counts "Compiling C object" AND "Compiling C++ object"' -- and fixed the denominator to match while leaving objs() as it was.
remediation: Widen to `grep -oE 'Compiling C(\+\+)? object [^ ]+'`. Cheap and makes the two halves of the same log agree.

summary: The header lookup is `grep -F "/$src"` against the deps list, which requires the warning's path to have at least one directory component.
scenario: A generated header sitting at the top of the build directory -- a config-host.h or qemu-version.h, which appear in deps as a bare filename with no leading slash -- cannot match, so its warnings are still dropped from the delta. Narrow residual of M3; the repo's own headers all live in subdirectories and are unaffected.
evidence: gate.sh:192. keyed() strips a leading '../' (:155-156) so repo-relative paths keep their directory component and match fine; it is only the no-directory case that falls through. Not exercised by my synthetic run, which used subdirectory headers -- stated rather than claimed as measured.
remediation: Match on the deps line's basename when $src has no '/', or anchor on the tab-separated second field rather than a substring.
